points.text: Incremental-session operations are generic (prototypes, projection); SNN-specific parts not shown to matter.
Zeroth-order optimization used only in base training.
Threshold update behaviour and its effect on forgetting never shown.
No matched-backbone ANN FSCIL baseline, so no evidence of SNN advantage.
Only base session trained on-device; unclear whether 300-epoch cost counts as on-device.
Gains largely from stronger base session; baseline backbone and tuning parity unstated.
Several baselines look implausibly weak or unstable.
Headline +4.01% gain is over a single baseline.
Ablation lacks plain SNN plus prototypes baseline.
Neuromorphic-dataset table compares only WARP and TEEN, reports only Avg and Last.
Table 3 parameter sizes are inconsistent and unexplained.
Claimed 20% energy reduction not matched by Fig. 4 (about 10%).
Energy measured on GPU reflects wall-clock time, not spike-based benefits.
Baseline for the 20% energy claim unspecified.
Speed-up attributed to training protocol, not the model.
Inference energy theoretical; no on-device memory or latency figures.
Eq. 14 projector singular when batch smaller than dimension; dimensions inconsistent.
G described as building distinct orthogonal subspaces but is a single projector.
Convergence claim does not follow for non-convex case; theory inherited, adds little.
No comparison of ZOO gradient quality or accuracy against surrogate-gradient training.
Notation and algorithm inconsistencies (tau/gamma, mask choice, loss description).
Threshold update needs stored base firing rate; overhead and update data unclear.
Neuromorphic 1-way 1-shot setting with few sessions is very small.
Novel-class and harmonic accuracy mostly absent; reported HAcc suggests poor novel accuracy.
Very small baseline standard deviations suggest seeds vary only session sampling.
Degradation on deep backbones like Spiking ResNet-34 limits scalability.
Text repetitive with grammar and word-choice problems.
Motivation overstates some points about existing systems and PEFT.
Figure 1 claims memory reduction but memory never measured.
Several claims supported only in appendix.
Why sparsity-aware dynamics keep most neurons stable is not explained.
Power evaluated theoretically rather than measured at runtime.
Figure 5 speed not significantly better than other methods.
Eq. 14 matrix multiplication makes neuromorphic-chip deployment nearly impossible.
Missing equation punctuation and poor Table 3 alignment.
ZOO lacks quantitative comparison with surrogate backpropagation and error-source analysis.
Degradation in deeper networks not explained or addressed.
Abstract and introduction vague; key terms not intuitively explained.
No comparison against ANN on-device FSCIL methods; SNN superiority unjustified.
Claim of alleviating novel-class overfitting insufficiently motivated.
Baseline for 20% energy claim unspecified.
Subspace projection advantages not shown versus other projection or regularization methods.
Sparsity-aware dynamics resemble subnet/SoftNet approaches; direct comparison missing.
Zeroth-order optimization not contrasted with other optimization methods.
Sparsity-aware alignment overlaps prior temporal-consistency and membrane-potential losses.
Sparsity-aware loss heuristic without formal derivation.
Ablation lacks sensitivity to sparsity thresholds and alignment weights.
No visual explanation of feature alignment beyond one layer.
No measured power or latency on neuromorphic hardware.
Robustness to noise, temporal jitter, or unseen sensor dynamics untested.
No mechanistic link between alignment and gradient flow or accuracy gains.
Effect of added loss on training convergence and stability unanalysed.
